discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms with Rydberg-blockade interactions for quantum simulation and quantum computing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Over twenty-five years, these physicists turned single atoms in optical tweezers into one of the most powerful platforms for controlled many-body quantum physics. Lukin (with Zoller and coworkers) proposed the Rydberg dipole blockade as a mechanism for entangling neutral atoms and later led the development of large reconfigurable atom arrays, logical qubits and the observation of quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquids. Saffman, with Walker, demonstrated the blockade between two individually trapped atoms and the first neutral-atom CNOT gate. Browaeys observed collective Rydberg excitation of two atoms, built defect-free assembled arrays in two and three dimensions, and used them to simulate quantum magnetism with hundreds of spins. Their work, from careful single-atom optics to programmable quantum matter, has opened a new route to quantum simulation and fault-tolerant computation, now taken up worldwide in laboratories and industry.
